newsitem.title: UK: Unilever posts 24 percent gain in income.
newsitem.headline: Unilever posts 24 percent gain in income.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever Plc/NV said Friday its six-month profit jumped an unexpected 24 percent to 1.374 billion pounds ($2.2 billion).

The 24 percent increase, which excluded profit from the sale of its speciality chemicals business to Imperial Chemical Industries Plc for $8 billion in early July, exceeded all stock market forecasts.

Analysts expected profits before tax in the second quarter, excluding the sale of speciality chemicals, of between 730 million ($1.19 billion) and 780 million ($1.28 billion) pounds compared with the actual 37 percent increase to 836 million ($1.37 billion).

Unilever Plc shares were 27 pence higher in London at 1,796p, and in Amsterdam Unilever N.V. gained 9.10 guilders to 464.10. The company also announced a proposed share split in both the British and Dutch arms on a four-for-one basis.
For the six months to June 30, the group made pre-tax profit of 4.39 billion pounds $(7.19 billion) including a 3.02 billion ($4.95 billion) profit from the sale of its speciality chemicals division.
Chairman Niall Fitzgerald said profits growth in the remainder of the year would be less buoyant and sales growth is likely to remain modest.
